title: Berlin Housing Cooperatives - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has more than 80 housing cooperatives holding roughly 190,000 flats**, out of about 1.65 million rented homes in the city. The ten largest hold 64,516 between them. It is a second housing market, and it does not work like the open one.

**You buy shares, you do not pay a landlord.** At Wohnungsgenossenschaft Treptower Park eG one share is 256 euros and a 62 square metre flat needs seven of them, so 1,792 euros, plus a 30 euro joining fee. At Berliner Bau- und Wohnungsgenossenschaft von 1892 membership alone is two shares of 300 euros plus a 300 euro joining fee, with more shares by flat size before you move in.

**The share money is not a deposit and it does not come back quickly.** The 1892 statutes require two years' notice to the end of a financial year, and the settlement is then calculated from that year's balance sheet. Give notice in spring 2027 and the money lands around 2030.

**The waiting list is the real price.** 1892 states on its own membership page that popular estates can mean ten years or more, and that you become a member when a flat is actually offered. Apply to eight or ten cooperatives years before you need one.

**The rent gap is modest on paper and large on a new contract.** The Berliner Mietspiegel 2026 average is 7.71 euros per square metre net cold, and BBU member companies averaged 7.10 euros on 30 June 2025. Against an open-market asking rent the difference is far bigger, which is where the share money actually pays for itself.

**Berlin will lend you the share money interest free.** The Investitionsbank Berlin funds first-time share purchases from 2,000 to 50,000 euros, writes off 15 percent at payout and another 10 percent near the end, over up to 30 years. It needs a valid Berlin Wohnberechtigungsschein.

**One simple move: apply now, decide later.** Membership enquiries cost nothing at most cooperatives until a flat is offered. Send them this month, then use the payback plotter when a real flat with a real rent turns up.
